title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
hook: One model that reads and generates language, images, video, audio, and actions — NVIDIA's open Cosmos 3 folds VLMs, video generators, and robot policies into a single backbone.
key_points: A mixture-of-transformers architecture that jointly processes and generates text, image, video, audio, and action sequences.
Subsumes vision-language models, video generators, world simulators, and world-action models in one framework.
Ranked best open Text-to-Image and Image-to-Video by Artificial Analysis, and best policy model by RoboArena at report time.
Code, checkpoints, synthetic datasets, and benchmarks released openly under the Linux Foundation's OpenMDW-1.1 license.
content_html: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 is a family of "omnimodal world models" built for Physical AI — robots and embodied agents that have to perceive and act in the real world. Rather than stitching together a separate vision-language model, a video generator, and a control policy, Cosmos 3 aims to be a single model that handles all of them.
extra_html:
What it is

Cosmos 3 uses a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture that can jointly process and generate language, image, video, audio, and action sequences, with flexible input-output configurations. That breadth lets one model play the roles usually split across vision-language models, video generators, world simulators, and world-action (control) models. NVIDIA reports state-of-the-art results across a suite of understanding and generation tasks, with post-trained variants ranked as the best open Text-to-Image and Image-to-Video models by Artificial Analysis and the best policy model by RoboArena at the time of writing.

Why it matters

The bet here is that a single omnimodal backbone — one that can both imagine futures (generate video) and act (output control sequences) — is a more scalable foundation for embodied agents than a pipeline of specialized models. Notably, NVIDIA released code, model checkpoints, curated synthetic datasets, and the evaluation benchmark openly under the Linux Foundation's OpenMDW-1.1 license, making it a substantial open contribution to physical-AI research.

related.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
related.hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.

related.title: DreamerV3: Mastering Domains through World Models
related.hook: Instead of learning only from real experience, DreamerV3 builds a world model and practices inside its own imagination — one fixed config, 150+ tasks.

related.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models
related.hook: Treat a robot's actions as just more text tokens, and a vision-language model can learn to act — carrying its web knowledge into the physical world.

prereqs.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
prereqs.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.
